extracted.intended_audience: literary readers, poets, public speakers, and general readers interested in Whitman's essays and reflections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative remarks about poetic ideals, the human voice, public speaking, and authentic composition drawn from Whitman's essays and reminiscences. Useful for writers, performers, and critics seeking aesthetic and performance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect human voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The human voice is a cultivation or form'd growth on a fair native foundation; the grand voice is mainly physiological (though mental help exists). Beyond other power and beauty, the quality and power of the right voice (timbre) touches the soul to its depths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize physiological cultivation of voice and timbre. Schools call it 'timbre'. Study celebrated exemplars (Alboni, Elias Hicks, Father Taylor, Bettini, Fanny Kemble, Booth) as models. Appreciate voice as primary means of poetic and philosophical utterance (as in ancient traditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: American poetry should be spiritual and democratic
rubrics_metrics.description: The Old World is the region of concrete, esthetic, historical poetry; the New World (America) is the region of the future, whose poetry must be spiritual and democratic. Evolution applies to verse as to politics and inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works that reflect a broadened, modernized sense of 'spirituality' and democratic outlook rather than merely imitating old-world concrete aesthetics; allow science as a determining critic for future poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid writing for the public; choose nature and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: No free and original lofty-soaring poem can be fulfilled by a writer who has largely in mind 'the public' or what established literature/authorities will say. Nature (in letter and spirit) should be the model rather than the well-tended garden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not tailor ambitious poetry to please current public tastes or authorities. Aim to arouse the latent capacities in each soul; prioritize originality, authenticity, and nature-derived inspiration over fashionable esthetic palates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit magazine acceptance criteria (what editors reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many pieces were returned by magazines with reasons such as being 'an improvisation' or 'personal merely'; editors frequently rejected works judged too improvisational or personal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting to periodicals, be aware that editors may favor pieces that appear crafted, generalizable, or less overtly personal—avoid leaving the impression of mere improvisation if seeking acceptance by mainstream monthlies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern oratory qualities (as exemplified by Ingersoll)
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful modern oration may be delivered altogether without notes, in a good voice (not too low), with an easy, colloquial style, direct address to the audience, occasional humor, marked passion, and interior fire and volition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for 40–50 minutes of material organized but delivered conversationally; use direct address ('you'), modulated voice, controlled passion, and well-placed humor. Presence of natural magnetism and vivacity enhances persuasive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public speaker/critic traits (William D. O'Connor example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power and a sharp-cut faculty of statement and persuasiveness, a remarkable physiologic voice, an idiosyncratic identity, and a catholic readiness to defend and welcome diverse masters characterize an admirable speaker and critic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate distinctive personal voice and style, sharpen rhetorical clarity and persuasiveness, and combine broad tolerance of literary variety with a clear individual standpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence valued over prepared address
rubrics_metrics.description: At certain public occasions, showing oneself face to face and following the impulse of the spirit (presence) can be preferable to making a formal speech; presence may be 'the best I can do.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that authentic presence, personal display of oneself, and spontaneous engagement can be more meaningful than delivering a prepared address; prioritize sincerity of encounter in some public contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old-style health ideal (description of vigorous, natural health)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health described as an elevated, inwardly and outwardly illuminated state: transparency in the eyes, buoyant strength, grace of motion, freedom from anticipatory sorrow, and delight in simple movement and sensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This portrayal serves as a model of bodily and mental vigor—valued traits for a writer/performer—advocating natural living, exercise, temperance, and an attitude that transforms hardships into sustaining strength.
